problem: Penetration is defined as 'how far the spray tip travels before it is fully broken up and mixed'. Breakup and mixing do not stop the spray tip; penetration is the maximum distance the tip reaches from the nozzle at a given time. A student may think penetration ends when atomisation finishes.
fix: Define penetration as the maximum distance the spray tip travels from the nozzle orifice into the chamber after start of injection, then say this distance must match the chamber.

problem: The wording 'the full angle between the spray edges, often 10° to 25° for multi-hole nozzles' can be read as the included angle of all jets from a multi-hole nozzle. The 10°–25° value is the cone angle of one individual jet; the included angle between the outer jets of a multi-hole nozzle is much larger.
fix: Say that the cone angle of an individual jet is often 10° to 25°, while the included angle between the outer jets of a multi-hole nozzle is much larger (for example, 140° to 160°).

problem: The Beyond note says production nozzles use holes of about 0.1 mm, but Section 1 gives the multi-hole range as 0.15 mm to 0.4 mm. The two statements conflict unless the text says the smaller holes are a modern development.
fix: State that modern high-pressure common-rail nozzles use smaller holes (about 0.08 mm to 0.12 mm), below the older 0.15 mm to 0.4 mm range given in Section 1.
